paragraphs.source_en: This time, the master turned his face aside again and looked at the half of it that caught the light in the mirror. As though he had discovered something, he said, “Seen like this, it stands out terribly. It looks smoother when the light comes straight from the front. How strange.” Then he stretched out the right arm that held the mirror, keeping it as far away as possible, and peered at it carefully for a long while. As if suddenly enlightened, he said, “At this distance it doesn’t show so much after all. Too close is no good. It isn’t only faces; everything is like that.” Next he suddenly turned the mirror sideways, and, using the bridge of his nose as the center, gathered his eyes, forehead, and eyebrows all toward that point. At a glance I saw a most disagreeable face; he too seemed to notice something and said, “No, this won’t do!” and at once stopped. “Why should it become such a vicious-looking face?” He muttered this, looking somewhat unconvinced, and drew his hand back again until the mirror was only three inches from his eyes. With the forefinger of his right hand he rubbed the side of his nose, then pressed the finger hard against the blotting paper on the desk. The grease wiped from his nose immediately appeared on the paper as a round mark. The master truly has all sorts of tricks to perform. Then the master turned that fingertip, now smeared with oil from his nose, and sharply pulled down his lower eyelid, neatly performing what people commonly call making a face by turning down the eyelid. Whether he was studying his pockmarks or competing with the mirror in a staring contest, one really could not tell. It seems the master is a man of changeable temper, and so, while I observe him, he contrives all manner of antics. Nor is that all. If one were to interpret it benevolently, though in a rather absurd and mismatched way, one might even suppose that the master was using the mirror as his opponent and performing these various gestures as a means toward seeing into his own nature and attaining enlightenment. For in truth, all research that human beings undertake is research into the self. Heaven and earth, mountains and rivers, sun, moon, and stars are all merely other names for oneself. No one can easily find any other matter to study apart from the self. If a person could leap outside his own circle, then at the very instant he leapt out, he would no longer be himself. Moreover, when it comes to studying oneself, no one but oneself will do it in one’s stead. However much he may want to do it for you, and however much you may want him to, it is all in vain. Thus the heroes of old all became heroes by their own strength. If one could understand oneself by relying on another, one could just as well ask a proxy to eat beef and then judge whether the beef was tough or tender. Hearing the Law in the morning and the Way in the evening, sitting before a paulownia-shaded window or beneath a lamp with book in hand, are all merely expedients for securing one’s own direct proof. In the doctrines preached by others, in the Zen way debated by others, and even amid the heaps of old papers and books enough to fill five carts, there is no place where one’s own self exists. If it is there at all, it is only the ghost of oneself.

paragraphs.source_zh: 这次，主人又别过脸去看他那照在镜子里半边受光的脸，他好像发现了什么似的说道：“这样看就很显眼，还是正面来光显得平些，真是怪啊。”然后他又把拿着镜子的右胳膊伸出去，尽量使镜子保持最远的距离，仔仔细细地瞧了老半天，好像恍然大悟似的说：“离开这么远，也就不怎么显眼啦，太近了是不行的，不只是脸，任何事情都是这样。”随后他又把镜子一下子横过来，而且以鼻梁为中心，使眼睛、额头、眉毛都向这个中心聚拢，我一眼看去，就看见了一个非常讨人厌的面孔，他本人似乎也有所发现，说了声“这不成！”便立刻停下来了。“为什么会成为这样一副恶狠狠的面孔呢？”他自语着，多少有些不太相信的样子，又把手缩回，到镜子离他的眼睛只有三寸远的地方，用右手的食指摸他的鼻翼，将摸过的手指在桌上的吸墨纸上狠狠地擦了一下从鼻头上抹下来的油脂，纸上立刻出现一个圆圆的印痕。主人真是会玩种种的把戏哩。然后，主人又把那涂抹过鼻子上油脂的手指头转过来，狠狠地扒了一下他的下眼皮，非常麻利地做了一个俗语说的“扒眼皮”的动作。也不知他是在研究麻子呢，还是在和镜子互相比赛瞪眼睛玩儿呢，真让人弄不清楚。看来，主人是个气性不定的人，所以在我观察他的时候，他会搞出各种花样儿来。还不只是这个，如果从善意出发，作点驴唇不对马嘴式的解释的话，那么也可以认为主人是作为“见性开悟”的一种手段，才这样以镜子为对手，大搞其种种动作呢。原来，人所进行的研究，其实都是在研究自身。无论是天地山川，还是日月星辰，无非是自己的别名。能够离开自己去研究的其他事项，是任何人也难以做到的。如果人能做到跳出自己的圈子，在跳出去的瞬间，人就已经不再是自己了。而且研究自己，除了自己以外，谁也不会代你去做。不管他怎样想代你做，你怎样想请他代你做，都是徒劳的。所以古来的豪杰都是用自己的力量成为豪杰，如果依靠别人能了解自己，那么也能做到请个代理人去吃牛肉，然后你能判断出牛肉是嫩是老了，那种“朝听法、夕闻道”，在梧桐窗前或灯下，手不释卷，都不过是采取目证的一种权宜之计罢了。在他人说法之中，他人论辩的禅道之中，乃至在富于五车的典籍、故纸堆中，都不会有自己的存在。如果有，那也只是自己的幽灵。

paragraphs.source_en: Of course, in certain cases a ghost is better than no spirit at all, and in pursuing a shadow one may not necessarily fail to encounter the substance. Many shadows, after all, scarcely depart from the substance. In that sense, if the master is fiddling with the mirror, he is still a man one can talk sense with. I think he is far better than those who swallow Epictetus whole and put on the airs of scholars.
